exercises.title: Brigade CPX: application unavailable
exercises.context: A fictional brigade CPX uses a generic training application. Several learners report they cannot access it.
learning_objectives: Distinguish service availability from transport reachability
Identify service owners and verification evidence

nodes.prompt: A fictional application is unavailable. What is the best initial approach?

choices.text: Define the affected users and collect symptoms

nodes.feedback: Avoid assigning a cause without evidence.

nodes.evidence: Users report the training site opens, but login fails. Network transport appears healthy in the simulation.
nodes.prompt: Which dependency should you investigate next?

nodes.feedback: Replacing unrelated components does not isolate a fault.

nodes.evidence: Synthetic identity health check reports unavailable; application service is running.
nodes.prompt: What is an appropriate training conclusion?

choices.text: Document evidence, involve the service owner, validate recovery

nodes.feedback: Successful access does not establish interoperability between different systems.
Completed. Root cause in this fictional scenario: identity service outage. The learner used symptoms and evidence to narrow the fault domain.

exercises.title: DIVARTY CPX: mission requirements discovery
exercises.context: A fictional fires staff requests support for several training systems. No interface compatibility has been verified.
learning_objectives: Separate system ownership from transport support

choices.text: Mission purpose, participants, data requirements and system owners
Assume all systems share a common interface

nodes.feedback: Shared networking technologies do not prove application interoperability.

nodes.evidence: The fictional staff identifies mission objectives and responsible system specialists. Specific versions and approved interfaces are unknown.

choices.text: Document unknowns and request authoritative version-specific evidence

nodes.feedback: Completed. Requirements and unknowns were documented without making unsupported compatibility claims.
